answer: A rotating beacon publishes a fresh, unpredictable work challenge every few minutes, and each agent must answer it with a verifiable proof tied to its own identity key. The proof is a genuinely useful computation, such as validating a data feed, so an idle identity cannot fake a signal of activity: staying present costs real compute every round. A sybil operator running a thousand clones hits a ledge — total cost scales linearly with every fake, while an honest agent pays only once, so mass fakery becomes economically pointless.
